cards.heading: Microcopy doubt injection — definition
cards.question: What is microcopy doubt injection?
cards.answer: The failure mode where small, operationally accurate phrases placed at high-stakes moments (fees, approvals, timing, consent) create hesitation disproportionate to the fact they state, because a reader at the point of commitment is scanning for reasons to stop.

cards.heading: Doubt injection — why placement matters
cards.question: Why does a phrase like 'processing fees may apply' matter more in one location than another?
cards.answer: Because damage scales with position — the phrase is harmless in help text but costly next to a payment button, where the reader is scanning for reasons to stop.

cards.heading: Doubt injection — phrase families
cards.question: Name three of the recognizable 'doubt families' that risky microcopy phrases cluster into.
cards.answer: Hidden-cost suspicion (e.g. 'processing fees'), rejection fear (e.g. 'subject to approval'), and delay anxiety (e.g. 'please allow up to'). Also: effort anxiety, privacy concern, and legalistic friction.

cards.heading: Doubt injection audit constraints
cards.question: What two constraints keep a microcopy doubt audit honest — one about required disclosures, one about replacement copy?
cards.answer: Required disclosures must be made clearer and more reassuring, never deleted; and no replacement may invent a guarantee, timeline, fee, or policy the business doesn't actually offer.

cards.heading: Doubt injection — evidence status
cards.question: What is the evidentiary status of the severity rankings in a microcopy doubt audit?
cards.answer: They are heuristics, not measured findings — the source reports no measured conversion lift, so rankings await A/B testing.
